title: Left Atrial Appendage Closure Is Inferior to Best Medical Therapy for Patients With Atrial Fibrillation and High Bleeding and Stroke Risk.
Clopidogrel-Based Versus Aspirin-Based Double Antithrombotic Therapy After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in Atrial Fibrillation Patients: Results of the ASAF-PCI Registry.
summary:
BACKGROUND: In patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), current guidelines recommend a brief period of triple antithrombotic therapy (TAT) consisting of an oral anticoagulant (OAC), aspirin and clopidogrel, followed by double antithrombotic therapy (DAT) with OAC plus clopidogrel. Evidence on aspirin as an alternative to clopidogrel within DAT remains limited.

AIMS: The present analysis aimed at describing contemporary use of aspirin- versus clopidogrel-based DAT and to compare 12-month clinical outcomes.

METHODS: In this multicenter, observational study, consecutive patients with AF undergoing PCI between January 2019 and December 2023 and discharged on DAT with OAC plus aspirin or clopidogrel were included. The primary endpoint was the 12-month incidence of net adverse clinical events (NACE), composite of all-cause death, non-fatal myocardial infarction (MI), non-fatal stroke, urgent revascularization, and major bleeding. Secondary composite and individual endpoints were also assessed. Multivariable logistic regression was used to adjust for baseline imbalances.

RESULTS: Among 445 patients, 291 (65.4%) were discharged on clopidogrel-based DAT and 154 (34.6%) on aspirin-based DAT. Baseline characteristics were largely comparable. NACE occurred in 15.1% versus 13.6% of patients (OR 1.13, 95% CI 0.64-1.98; p = 0.674), with no significant difference after multivariable adjustment (adjusted OR 1.15, 95% CI 0.59-2.26; p = 0.677). No significant between group differences were observed for secondary composite or individual efficacy and safety endpoints.

CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world cohort of AF patients undergoing PCI, aspirin- and clopidogrel-based DAT with OAC were not associated with significantly different 12-month outcomes. These hypothesis-generating findings require confirmation in adequately powered randomized trials.

title: Sex-Based Disparities in the In-Hospital Outcomes and Resource Utilization of Atrial Fibrillation in Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) frequently coexist and may amplify cardiovascular and respiratory morbidity. However, sex-specific differences in inpatient outcomes and resource utilization among patients with both conditions remain incompletely characterized.

METHODS: We performed a nationwide retrospective analysis of the 2016-2022 National Inpatient Sample (NIS), identifying adult hospitalizations with AF and COPD using ICD-10-CM codes. Weighted estimates were used to obtain national inpatient estimates. Baseline characteristics, in-hospital mortality, length of stay (LOS), inflation-adjusted hospital costs, and discharge disposition were compared by sex. Multivariable regression models adjusted for demographic, socioeconomic, hospital, and comorbidity-related factors.

RESULTS: Among 1 475 163 unweighted hospitalizations representing more than 7.37 million weighted discharges, 52.9% involved males. Females were older and more frequently admitted emergently, whereas males had a higher prevalence of several cardiovascular and renal comorbidities. In-hospital mortality was 5.8% in males and 5.4% in females. After multivariable adjustment, male sex remained associated with higher in-hospital mortality (aOR 1.039, 95% CI 1.024-1.054), shorter LOS (regression coefficient -0.085, 95% CI -0.106 to -0.064), higher hospital cost (+$854.95, 95% CI +$778.80 to +$931.10), and lower odds of discharge to a skilled nursing facility (aOR 0.790, 95% CI 0.784-0.796).

CONCLUSIONS: Substantial sex-based differences exist in comorbidity profiles, inpatient outcomes, and resource utilization among adults hospitalized with AF and COPD. These findings support greater attention to sex-specific risk assessment and discharge planning. Because the NIS is an administrative inpatient database, the observed associations should not be interpreted as causal and do not capture outpatient or post-discharge outcomes.

title: Case Report: Isoproterenol-dependent concealed right anteroseptal accessory pathway.
summary: A 34-year-old male with no history of chronic medical illness or regular medication use presented with recurrent palpitations, chest tightness, and presyncope over two weeks. A wearable smart device recorded brief runs of irregular narrow-complex tachycardia, which were initially misdiagnosed as paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. During baseline electrophysiological study (EPS), ventriculoatrial (VA) conduction exhibited Wenckebach periodicity; no accessory pathway (AP) was identified, and no supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) could be induced. Following intravenous isoproterenol (ISO) infusion, retrograde conduction improved, and narrow-complex tachycardia was successfully induced via programmed stimulation [S1S2 coupling intervals of 330/210 milliseconds (ms)] from the coronary sinus. Orthodromic atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia (AVRT) was confirmed. The concealed AP was localized to the right anteroseptal region (specifically, the 12-1 o'clock position on the tricuspid annulus) and was successfully ablated using radiofrequency energy. Post-ablation EPS demonstrated non-inducibility of tachycardia. The patient remained free of arrhythmia recurrence during 18 months of clinical follow-up. This case illustrates a rare isoproterenol-dependent concealed right anteroseptal AP and underscores the diagnostic utility of ISO provocation in patients with narrow-complex tachycardia when arrhythmia is not induced on standard EPS.

title: Device-detected new-onset atrial fibrillation after dual-chamber pacemaker implantation in patients with sick sinus syndrome under managed ventricular pacing: a risk nomogram from the 3-month landmark.
summary:
BACKGROUND: New-onset atrial fibrillation (NOAF) is common after dual-chamber pacemaker implantation, but existing prediction models were derived from mixed populations of patients with sick sinus syndrome (SSS) and atrioventricular block and included heterogeneous pacing strategies.

METHODS: In this single-centre retrospective cohort study, consecutive patients with SSS who received a first permanent Medtronic dual-chamber pacemaker with managed ventricular pacing (MVP) enabled as the default strategy were screened. Patients with atrial fibrillation or an atrial high-rate episode (AHRE) within 3 months after implantation were excluded, and prediction time started at this 3-month landmark, with atrial pacing percentage (AP%) and ventricular pacing percentage (VP%) measured at that visit. Patients implanted in 2015-2021 formed the development cohort (n = 322), and those implanted in 2022-2025 formed a temporal validation cohort (n = 121) reserved exclusively for validation. Twenty-six candidate predictors were assessed by univariable and multivariable Cox regression with backward Akaike information criterion (AIC) selection. Internal validation repeated the complete model-building procedure within 2,000 bootstrap samples. Temporal performance was assessed using discrimination and calibration at 1, 2 and 3 years after the landmark.

RESULTS: NOAF occurred in 90 of 322 development patients (28.0%) during a median follow-up of 41.6 months [interquartile range (IQR), 13.7-80.1], and in 28 of 121 temporal validation patients (23.1%) during a median follow-up of 30.5 months (IQR, 8.8-45.9). Age (hazard ratio [HR] per year, 1.043; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.019-1.067), maximum P-wave duration (Pmax; HR per 10 ms, 1.200; 95% CI, 1.085-1.326), left atrial volume index (LAVi; HR per 1 mL/m2, 1.051; 95% CI, 1.030-1.073), AP% > 50% (HR, 1.845; 95% CI, 1.198-2.840) and VP% > 40% (HR, 1.898; 95% CI, 1.045-3.446) were independently associated with NOAF. The apparent C-index was 0.735; repeating the complete model-building procedure within 2,000 bootstrap samples gave a mean optimism of 0.036 and an optimism-corrected C-index of 0.6992. In temporal validation the C-index was 0.769 (95% CI, 0.639-0.873) and cumulative/dynamic AUC values were 0.753, 0.881 and 0.916 at 1, 2 and 3 years after the landmark. Calibration-in-the-large was -0.17, 0.24 and 0.35 and calibration slopes were 0.90, 0.99 and 0.98 at 1, 2 and 3 years, respectively. The 1-year calibration estimate remained least precise, with only five NOAF events by 1 year in the validation cohort.

CONCLUSION: In patients with SSS who remained free of atrial arrhythmia through the 3-month post-implantation landmark, a five-variable landmark model showed moderate optimism-corrected discrimination in the development cohort and promising same-centre temporal validation performance, particularly at 2 and 3 years after the landmark. The limited number of validation events, particularly at 1 year, warrants cautious interpretation. Prospective multicentre external validation is required before clinical implementation.

title: Rising Atrial Fibrillation Mortality Trends in Hypertensive Patients Aged 25 and Older: A CDC Wonder Database Analysis.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is a leading arrhythmia contributing to cardiovascular mortality, particularly among individuals with Hypertension (HTN), yet long-term trends and disparities remain underexplored. We analyzed national patterns and sociodemographic differences in AF-related mortality among US adults aged 25 years or older from 1999 to 2023.

METHODS: We used CDC WONDER mortality data (1999-2023) to analyze AF-related deaths among US adults aged ≥ 25 with HTN. Age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMR) per 100 000 and average annual percent changes (AAPC) were calculated using Joinpoint regression to assess overall and subgroup-specific trends.

RESULTS: AF accounted for 1 108 265 deaths among adults with HTN, with AAMRs increasing from 3.8 in 1999 to 35.9 in 2023 (AAPC: 6.03%). The sharpest rise occurred from 2018 to 2021, with an APC of 14.57%, coinciding with the COVID-19 pandemic. Men had higher AAMRs than women (20.5 vs. 17.1). Racial disparities were evident, with non-Hispanic Whites having the highest AAMR (20.1), followed by non-Hispanic Blacks (15.1), Hispanics (11.3), and non-Hispanic Others (10.7). Regional variation showed that the West had the highest AAMR (20.8), while Vermont recorded the highest state rate (28.7), and Nevada had the lowest (11.4). Rural areas exhibited higher mortality rates than urban areas (17.8 vs. 16.1), with rural AAMRs increasing at a faster rate (AAPC: 10.61%).

CONCLUSION: The rising burden of AF-related mortality in hypertensive patients, especially among men, non-Hispanic Whites, and rural populations, signals a critical public health concern. Immediate, equity-focused interventions are needed to mitigate disparities and reduce AF-related mortality across the United States.

title: Antithrombotic Prescribing Pattern and Predictors of Oral Anticoagulants Use in Patients with Atrial Fibrillation: Results from a hospital-based cross-sectional study of Nepal.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) are at an increased risk of stroke and require oral anticoagulants (OACs) to reduce the risk of stroke and improve clinical outcomes. Guidelines do not recommend antiplatelet therapy without a specific indication; however, its use persists in clinical practice. Identifying the factors associated with oral anticoagulants use may help optimize patient care.

OBJECTIVE: To assess the antithrombotic use pattern and predictors of oral anticoagulant use.

METHOD: This cross-sectional study included patients aged ≥ 18 years with atrial fibrillation who attended the cardiopulmonary unit of the Dhulikhel Hospital, Kathmandu University Hospital, from March 2022 to April 2023. Stroke risk was assessed using the CHA2DS2-VASc score. Patients taking antiplatelet agents, vitamin K antagonists, and non-vitamin K antagonists were considered to be receiving antithrombotic therapy. Binary logistic regression was performed to identify the predictors of oral anticoagulant use.

RESULT: Among 215 patients with atrial fibrillation, 63.2% were receiving oral anticoagulants, and 30.2% were on antiplatelet therapy. Within the oral anticoagulant group, rivaroxaban was the most commonly used (38.6%). Among patients classified as high risk of stroke, 61.8% were on oral anticoagulants, whereas 32.8% were on antiplatelet therapy. Congestive heart failure, coronary artery disease, and moderate-to-severe bleeding risk were identified as significant predictors of oral anticoagulant use among patients atrial fibrillation (p < 0.05).

CONCLUSION: Many patient atrial fibrillation were prescribed oral anticoagulants to prevent stroke; however, antiplatelet therapy continues to be administered. Congestive heart failure, coronary artery disease, and elevated bleeding risk predicted of oral anticoagulant use. These findings underscore the importance of optimizing oral anticoagulant therapy according to individual patient risk profiles.

title: Hemoglobin glycation index and mortality in critically ill atrial fibrillation patients: A retrospective cohort study from the MIMIC‑IV database.
summary: The hemoglobin glycation index (HGI), a marker of individual glycation propensity, has demonstrated prognostic value in cardiometabolic diseases. Its association with outcomes in critically ill patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) remains poorly characterized, particularly over the longer term. In this retrospective cohort study, we analyzed data from 2458 ICU patients with AF in the MIMIC-IV database. HGI was calculated as the difference between measured glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) and the value predicted from fasting plasma glucose. The primary endpoints were 30-day and 365-day all-cause mortality. We employed Kaplan-Meier analysis, Cox proportional hazards models, restricted mean survival time (RMST), and restricted cubic splines. Subgroup analyses were exploratory. Prespecified sensitivity analyses addressed bias via exclusion of continuous enteral/parenteral nutrition or dextrose fluids, restriction of HbA1c to within 7 days, exclusion of recent transfusion or extreme hemoglobin, and a lipid complete-case analysis. The analysis revealed a reverse J-shaped relationship between HGI and all-cause mortality. Patients in the lowest HGI quartile (Q1) faced the highest risk of death across all time points. RMST was significantly shorter in Q1 versus Q2. Adjusted spline curves confirmed this nonlinear association, with inflection points at HGI values of -0.54 (30-day) and -0.65 (365-day). In the fully adjusted model, the Q2 versus Q1 hazard ratio (HR) was 0.704 (95% CI: 0.530-0.933) for 30-day and 0.714 (0.552-0.924) for 365-day mortality. Directionally consistent estimates were observed across all sensitivity analyses, for example, excluding enteral/parenteral nutrition [0.641 (0.464-0.885)], restricting HbA1c to 7 days [0.611 (0.408-0.913)], excluding transfusion/extreme hemoglobin [0.713 (0.527-0.964)], and lipid complete-case [0.647 (0.455-0.920)]. Subgroup analyses did not identify significant effect modification after FDR correction; however, these analyses were underpowered. In this MIMIC-IV cohort of critically ill AF patients, HGI exhibits a reverse J-shaped association with mortality, indicating that low HGI, and to a lesser extent high HGI, may identify higher-risk phenotypes. These findings require external validation and should not be interpreted causally. Integrating HGI into initial metabolic profiling could enhance risk stratification and inform personalized monitoring strategies in the ICU, pending prospective confirmation.

title: MRI-Derived Atrial Substrate Score Predicts Recurrence After First-Time Cryoballoon Pulmonary Vein Isolation.
summary:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The conventional classification of atrial fibrillation (AF) as paroxysmal or persistent may not reflect structural atrial remodeling and has limited value for predicting recurrence after pulmonary vein isolation (PVI). We investigated whether an MRI-derived substrate score combining left atrial (LA) fibrosis and size improves recurrence risk stratification after first-time cryoballoon PVI.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 69 patients undergoing first cryoballoon PVI; 67 underwent pre-procedural 3-Tesla late gadolinium enhancement MRI. LA fibrosis was graded using the UTAH classification; the maximal horizontal LA diameter in the two-chamber view was measured, and LA volume was calculated with a 3D tool. An exploratory point-based score was constructed from LA diameter categories (< 44 mm, 0 points; 44-< 48 mm, 2 points; ≥ 48 mm, 4 points) and advanced fibrosis (UTAH stage 3-4, 1 point). Discrimination for 12-month arrhythmia recurrence was assessed by ROC analysis.

RESULTS: Advanced fibrosis was present in half of the patients with paroxysmal AF, with a similar UTAH distribution in both phenotypes (p = 0.83). LA diameter and volume were larger in patients with recurrence and discriminated recurrence (AUC 0.95 and 0.92). The substrate score predicted recurrence (AUC 0.96, 95% CI 0.91-0.99), with recurrence rates of 0%, 41% and 96% in low-, intermediate- and high-risk patients. LA size was the main contributor, with fibrosis providing complementary information, whereas AF phenotype did not provide incremental predictive value.

CONCLUSIONS: An MRI-derived substrate score, with LA size as the main contributor and fibrosis as a complementary marker, predicted arrhythmia recurrence after cryoballoon PVI better than the conventional AF phenotype. External validation is required before clinical implementation.

title: Left Atrial Appendage Function vs. Geometry: Predicting Thrombus Risk in Atrial Fibrillation.
summary:
OBJECTIVE: Left atrial appendage (LAA) thrombus and/or spontaneous echo contrast (SEC) may occur despite adequate anticoagulation in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF). This study aimed to evaluate whether mitral annular geometry (annular area and sphericity) and the angle between the mitral annular plane and the Coumadin ridge are associated with LAA thrombus and/or SEC in anticoagulated patients with AF.

METHOD: We retrospectively enrolled 133 consecutive patients with AF (≥2 years' duration) receiving anticoagulant therapy who were referred for ablation or cardioversion. Preprocedural TEE provided measurements of LAA fractional area change (FAC), flow velocity, MAP-Coumadin ridge angle, mitral annular area, and sphericity. Logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors of thrombus/SEC.

RESULTS: LAA thrombus/SEC was present in 44 patients (33.1%). Compared with unaffected patients, those with thrombus/SEC had lower LAA FAC (0.26+-0.13 vs. 0.37+-0.12, P < 0.001), a larger mitral annular area (992.50+-210.81 vs. 898.75+-159.04 mm², P = 0.009), lower LVEF, more frequent heart failure, and larger cardiac dimensions. The MAP-LAA angle and sphericity were similar between the groups. On multivariable analysis, LAA FAC was the sole independent predictor (OR 0.49 per 10% increment, 95% CI 0.32-0.70, P < 0.001; AUC 0.72, cutoff 0.20, sensitivity 44%, specificity 96%). Mitral annular area showed modest discriminatory ability (AUC 0.64) and did not significantly improve the model when combined with FAC (P = 0.39).

CONCLUSION: LAA FAC is a strong independent predictor of thrombus/SEC in anticoagulated patients with AF, underscoring the primacy of appendage contractile function over geometric parameters. Mitral annular enlargement provides only marginal incremental value, whereas the MAP-LAA angle does not contribute. Routine measurement of LAA FAC provides a simple, reproducible echocardiographic tool for thrombus risk stratification.

title: Distinct Sex-Associated Phenotypes of Sudden Cardiac Arrest Across Clinical, ECG, and Echocardiographic Domains: Replication in Two Communities and Comparison with the Framingham Heart Study.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Sex differences in sudden cardiac arrest (SCA) incidence and outcomes are well established, but risk stratification underperforms in women. It is important to delineate sex-specific patterns in SCA across clinical, electrocardiographic, and echocardiographic domains.

METHODS: We studied out-of-hospital SCA cases from the Oregon Sudden Unexpected Death Study (ORSUDS; Portland, 2002-2020; discovery) and Prediction of Sudden Death in Multi-Ethnic Communities (PRESTO; Ventura County, 2015-2024; external replication). Sex differences in 38 comorbidities, 19 ECG and 12 echocardiographic measures were estimated using multivariable-adjusted logistic regression. Female sex was the modeled dependent measure (male as reference). ORSUDS estimates were compared with those in the Framingham Heart Study (FHS), a community-based reference cohort, using FDR-adjusted Cochran Q tests.

RESULTS: Among 5130 ORSUDS cases, 1715 (33.4%) were women (median age, 70.4 years [IQR, 58.7-81.8]) and 3415 (66.6%) were men (65.6 [55.0-76.8]). Compared with men, women had higher BMI (per 5 kg/m², 1.11 [1.08-1.15]) and higher odds of thyroid disease (2.56 [2.17-3.13]), asthma (2.33 [1.92-2.86]), mood disorder (2.17 [1.85-2.50]), dementia (1.27 [1.02-1.56]), and left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH, 3.13 [2.44-4.00]). Women also had lower odds of coronary artery disease (0.61 [0.52-0.71]), atrial fibrillation (0.67 [0.56-0.79]), prolonged QTc (0.45 [0.35-0.57]), prolonged PR (0.53 [0.41-0.68]), premature contractions (0.77 [0.60-0.98]), sleep apnea (0.53 [0.43-0.65]), and reduced LVEF (0.40 [0.29-0.54]). Most findings were replicated in PRESTO (n=2719). In contrast, several of these differences were reversed in the community (FHS, n=3539;FDR-significant): prolonged QTc was more common in women, whereas LVH, dementia, heart failure, and higher BMI were more common in men.

CONCLUSIONS: Sex differences among SCA cases were mostly reproducible in SCA cohorts, and distinct from sex-related patterns in the community. These results have implications for development of sex-specific SCA risk assessment and prevention strategies.

CLINICAL PERSPECTIVE: What is new?: This study is the first community-based analysis to comprehensively characterize pre-arrest sex-associated profiles across clinical, ECG, and echocardiographic domains, externally validate them, and compare them with a community reference population.Women with SCA were more strongly associated with non-cardiac comorbidities, LVH, preserved LVEF, and mitral valve abnormalities, whereas male cases were characterized by coronary and peripheral vascular disease, atrial fibrillation, prolonged PR and QTc intervals, premature contractions, and reduced LVEF.Several sex associations, including QTc prolongation, LVH, body mass index, heart failure, and dementia, differed in magnitude or direction from patterns in the community reference population.What are the clinical implications?: Our findings suggest candidate features for future sex specific risk factor analyses and potential components for sex-specific risk models for SCA.Clinicians may need to recognize the critical need to extend beyond dependence on just the value of the left ventricular ejection fraction for SCA risk prediction, especially in women.

title: AF/AFL-related hospitalizations in a provincial Chinese discharge-record database, 2016-2024: a retrospective observational study.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation and atrial flutter (AF/AFL) commonly coexist with older age and multimorbidity. Temporal changes in discharge-record counts are difficult to interpret when database coverage and recurrent admissions also change.

METHODS: We analyzed 2016-2024 hospital discharge front-page records with an I48 code in any of 16 diagnosis fields. Seven procedure code-name pairs were reviewed. We quantified annual institution coverage, repeated admissions among valid de-identified patient identifiers, and outcomes stratified by primary versus secondary AF/AFL diagnosis. Stable-institution analyses included 1,514 institutions reporting in every study year. Patient-cluster-robust logistic models were fitted in two layers: a baseline model using calendar year, demographics, diagnosis position, and mutually defined diagnosis groups, and an extended descriptive model adding in-hospital ventilation, dialysis, and cardiac ablation-related procedures.

RESULTS: The cohort comprised 2,868,578 AF/AFL-related hospitalizations from 1,098,442 valid unique patients and 5,069 institutions. Annual records increased from 142,305 in 2016 to 501,878 in 2024 (252.7%); records from the stable 1,514-institution subset increased from 137,063 to 443,780 (223.8%). Among admissions with valid patient identifiers, subsequent admissions increased from 26.4% in 2016 to 70.9% in 2024. AF/AFL was primary in 132,018 admissions (4.6%). Primary-diagnosis admissions had lower in-hospital death (0.32% vs. 2.47%), shorter median length of stay (7 vs. 8 days), and more cardiac ablation-related procedures (25.7% vs. 0.33%) than secondary-diagnosis admissions. In baseline models, calendar year was associated with lower odds of death (aOR 0.91, 95% CI 0.91-0.91) and death/DAMA (aOR 0.93, 95% CI 0.93-0.93). Associations changed after adding post-admission interventions, including calendar-year aORs of 0.88 (0.87-0.88) and 0.91 (0.91-0.91), respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: AF/AFL-related discharge records increased in both the full and stable-institution cohorts, but the study cannot separate database expansion, repeated admissions, coding change, and population-level disease trends. The findings describe hospital-record patterns rather than incidence or population burden. Primary and secondary AF/AFL diagnosis admissions represent clinically different administrative strata, and adjusted associations should not be interpreted causally.

title: Ultrasound-guided Stellate Ganglion Block for Refractory Electrical Storm and Acute Upper Limb Ischemia.
summary: Electrical storm (ES) and acute upper limb ischemia are life-threatening emergencies in which sympathetic activation may contribute to ventricular arrhythmogenicity and peripheral vasoconstriction. This case series describes the response to ultrasound-guided stellate ganglion block (SGB) in seven patients presenting to the emergency department: four with acute upper limb ischemia and three with refractory ventricular tachycardia (VT)/ES. SGB was performed at the C6 vertebral level using 0.25% bupivacaine (6-8 mL). All patients showed improvement after the procedure. In patients with limb ischemia, pain scores decreased, with improvement in limb warmth, capillary refill, and distal perfusion. In patients with refractory VT/ES, the frequency of VT episodes decreased and hemodynamic stability improved. No major procedural complications were observed. Ultrasound-guided SGB may be considered an adjunctive bedside intervention in selected patients with refractory ventricular tachyarrhythmias or acute upper limb ischemia, potentially serving as a temporizing measure while definitive treatment is being arranged or undertaken.

title: Dynamic Risk Assessment of Severe Ventricular Arrhythmia in Patients With Implantable Defibrillators and Reduced Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Device shocks are associated with an adverse prognosis in patients with implantable cardioverter-defibrillators. This study aimed to develop and validate a predictive model based on dynamic changes in intracardiac electrograms to assess the risk of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia or ventricular fibrillation (VF) events in patients with implantable cardioverter-defibrillators and heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF).

METHODS: Experimental studies were conducted in pigs with HFrEF (N=8) to characterize intracardiac electrogram and surface ECG changes during HF decompensation. Sham-operated animals (N=6) were used as controls. In patients, the study used data from 2 independent cohorts of patients with ICDs. The first cohort included 5089 patients from 50 centers (199 218 tracings), leveraging electrical parameters associated with HFrEF decompensation in the experimental model to train and internally validate a dynamic convolutional neural network model for polymorphic ventricular tachycardia/VF prediction. External validation was performed in a second cohort of 2040 patients from 7 centers (369 845 tracings).

RESULTS: In pigs, HFrEF decompensation was associated with QRS prolongation on surface ECG tracings and reduced bipolar R-wave amplitude in intracardiac electrograms. Hemodynamic and electrical alterations of HFrEF decompensation significantly increased the risk of inducible VF episodes compared with sham-operated controls (87.5% versus 0%, respectively; P<0.001). In a clinical setting, a convolutional neural network-derived model predicted first VF or polymorphic ventricular tachycardia events by analyzing temporal patterns of R-wave amplitude, QRS duration, and premature ventricular complex burden. This approach yielded areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.787 (0.753-0.817) for the training cohort and 0.725 (0.709-0.739) for the external validation cohort. Dynamic risk prediction using the convolutional neural network model significantly outperformed static risk assessment based on clinical variables (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, 0.617 [0.602-0.632]).

CONCLUSIONS: A convolutional neural network-derived model, grounded in the pathophysiology of HFrEF, provides dynamic risk assessment of VF or polymorphic ventricular tachycardia events in patients with implantable cardioverter-defibrillator devices.

title: Real-World Positivity, Procedural Events, and Management Changes After Intravenous Methylergometrine Provocation Testing for Coronary Vasospasm: A Single-Center Study of 139 Patients.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Intracoronary acetylcholine is the reference agent for coronary spasm provocation, but intravenous ergot derivatives remain in use in several European centres, with limited contemporary data on their positivity rate in current clinical practice.

AIMS: To assess the operator-defined positivity rate, procedural events, and associated changes in medical management following intravenous methylergometrine provocation.

METHODS: All coronary angiograms performed at a single centre between January 2025 and July 2026 were screened through a mandatory regional registry. Provocation consisted of a single 0.20-mg intravenous bolus of methylergometrine, with vasodilator therapy withdrawn 72 hours beforehand. The primary analysis was restricted to the first test performed in each patient. Medical treatment before and after provocation was compared using exact tests for paired data.

RESULTS: Among 2168 coronary angiograms screened, 152 provocation tests were performed in 139 patients. Among the 139 first tests, 28 were considered positive by the operator (20.1%; 95% confidence interval, 13.8-27.8%), while 14 fulfilled all three international diagnostic criteria. Current smoking was the only characteristic nominally associated with positivity (64.3% vs. 36.9%), although this association did not remain significant after correction for multiple comparisons. Transient events occurred during seven positive tests, including three self-terminating episodes of non-sustained ventricular tachycardia; none required cardioversion or vasopressor support. Vasodilator therapy was initiated or intensified after all 28 positive tests compared with 7 of 111 negative tests (6.3%). An alternative diagnosis was retained after 75 of 111 negative tests (67.6%).

CONCLUSIONS: Intravenous methylergometrine provocation was associated with operator-defined positivity in approximately one fifth of patients undergoing a first test and was consistently followed by the initiation or intensification of vasodilator therapy. Transient events occurred during a quarter of positive tests, and all resolved without cardioversion or vasopressor support; because procedure reports were retrievable for only a subset of negative tests, no cohort-wide safety estimate can be derived.

title: Buckled Silver Microflake Conductors With In Situ-Generated Ag-O Coordination Enable 3D-Printed Stretchable Cardiac Bioelectrodes.
summary: Metallic pacemaker electrodes risk myocardial injury during implantation, while silver micro-flakes (AgMFs), despite excellent conductivity, are too rigid for stretchable devices without proper composite/device engineering. Here, we present a synergistic strategy to fabricate fully stretchable, electrically stable, and crack-resistant cardiac electrodes by integrating AgMF-based ink with metal-organic interfacial bonding, biaxial buckling, and wet-adhesive hydrogels. In situ-generated Ag-O coordination of silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) in the polymer matrix/conductor dissipates stress and suppresses crack propagation, effectively compensating for AgMF rigidity and enabling intact buckled microstructures. The resulting electrodes exhibit high conductivity (∼2.1 × 104 S cm-1) and stable resistance under 50% cyclic strain, exceeding cardiac motion requirements (15%-20%). The ink is 3D-printable into mesh electrodes and can be integrated with wet-adhesive hydrogels to form puncture-free, stretchable metallic cardiac bioelectrodes with excellent biosafety, offering a promising route toward leadless pacemakers and long-term wireless cardiac monitoring. A multiscale synergistic strategy integrating metal-organic interfacial bonding with stretch-release-induced buckled architectures enables silver microflake conductors with simultaneously high conductivity and large deformability, demonstrated for 3D printing of bioadaptive, puncture-free cardiac electrodes and stretchable wireless coils for dynamic cardiac stimulation and long-term electrophysiological monitoring.

title: Conduction system versus biventricular pacing for cardiac resynchronization: A meta-analysis of randomized trials
summary: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials comparing conduction system pacing (His bundle pacing or left bundle branch area pacing) with biventricular pacing in adults with heart failure, reduced left ventricular ejection fraction and an indication for cardiac resynchronization therapy. The primary outcome is the between-group difference in change in left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF). Secondary outcomes are left ventricular end-systolic volume, all-cause death, heart failure hospitalisation, death or heart failure event, procedure-related complications, and procedure and fluoroscopy times. We test whether conduction system pacing is non-inferior to biventricular pacing for LVEF change, and whether trial-level delivery factors (pacing modality, crossover and trial scale) explain between-trial heterogeneity. This registration is retrospective: the literature search (1 November 2026), data extraction and analyses had been completed before registration. Analyses not specified at the outset (the non-inferiority test and trial scale as a moderator) are identified as such in the manuscript.

title: Left bundle branch area pacing in atrial fibrotic cardiomyopathy manifesting as atrial standstill: two case reports and mechanistic insights.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Atrial standstill (AS) is a rare arrhythmogenic disorder characterized by the complete absence of atrial electrical and mechanical activity, most commonly resulting from atrial fibrotic cardiomyopathy (AFC). Optimal management remains challenging, particularly when selecting an appropriate pacing strategy. Left bundle branch area pacing (LBBaP) provides physiological ventricular activation; however, its role in patients with AS is not well established.

CASE PRESENTATION: We report two patients managed with tailored LBBaP. Case 1: A 41-year-old female with biatrial electrical silence confirmed by 3D electroanatomic mapping received a single-chamber LBBaP pacemaker (implant-paced LVAT 71.97 ms; QRS narrowed from 124 to 93 ms). Case 2: A 36-year-old male, underwent dual-chamber pacing with an atrial septal lead and an LBBaP. After pacing, the pulmonary arterial systolic pressure decreased from 44 mmHg (native rhythm) to 27 mmHg.

DISCUSSION: AS management requires a thorough electrophysiological study to characterize the atrial substrate, which directly dictates the pacing strategy. Diffuse fibrosis necessitates single-chamber LBBaP to ensure ventricular synchrony, whereas localized viability allows dual-chamber pacing to restore atrioventricular synchrony. Anticoagulation is mandatory owing to the high thromboembolic risk, irrespective of the pacing mode.

TAKE HOME MESSAGES: AS management requires a substrate-guided approach. LBBaP represents a physiologically aligned alternative to conventional RVP; however, head-to-head comparative evidence is required. Atrial lead implantation is feasible in cases of localized viable tissue. Anticoagulation is mandatory regardless of the pacing mode.

title: Iatrogenic axillary arteriovenous fistula complicating permanent pacemaker implantation: successful management with a balloon-expandable covered stent-a case report.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Third-degree atrioventricular block is a class I indication for permanent pacemaker implantation. Iatrogenic axillary arteriovenous fistula is an extremely rare vascular complication of this procedure with limited clinical reports to date.

CASE PRESENTATION: We present the case of a 57-year-old male with third-degree atrioventricular block who developed an axillary arteriovenous fistula during permanent pacemaker implantation via the left axillary vein approach. The complication was promptly diagnosed by emergency axillary arteriography and was successfully occluded with an 8 mm × 37 mm balloon-expandable covered stent. Owing to the ipsilateral vascular injury, the pre‑created left pacemaker pocket was then closed in layers. Permanent pacemaker implantation was subsequently completed uneventfully via the contralateral right axillary vein approach, with a new pacemaker pocket created on the right side. The patient had an uncomplicated postoperative course and normal pacemaker function at the 1-month follow-up, with no recurrence of symptoms or vascular abnormalities.

CONCLUSIONS: We review the relevant literature, analyze the pathophysiology, diagnosis and interventional management of this rare complication, and propose clinical recommendations for its prevention and acute management, including rational pacemaker pocket management after successful vascular fistula occlusion. This case reinforces the efficacy and safety of balloon-expandable covered stents for iatrogenic axillary arteriovenous fistula and highlights the importance of multidisciplinary collaboration, prompt angiographic diagnosis, and deliberate pocket selection in the management of such acute procedural complications.

title: Neural Architecture Search-Based ECG Classification for Low-Power Edge Deployment in IoT Healthcare Systems.
summary:
OBJECTIVE: To develop and validate a deployment-centric ECG arrhythmia classification framework for low-power wearable edge devices, with emphasis on efficient on-device screening and reduced communication burden in remote cardiac monitoring workflows, optimized for seamless integration into clinical remote monitoring workflows using resource-constrained wearable IoT edge devices.

METHODS AND PROCEDURES: We design a clinically-oriented wearable-to-phone workflow in which the edge device performs on-device ECG inference and transmits actionable anomaly summaries to a smartphone via Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE). This approach reduces latency, energy cost, and privacy risks compared to continuous raw-signal transmission. A NAS process tailored to arrhythmia detection automatically explores candidate architectures under diverse compute and memory constraints to identify feasible models for embedded platforms. Multiple deployment-ready variants are generated via quantization and pruning, and implemented on an ARM Cortex-M33-based system. System efficiency is quantified through end-to-end measurements of energy consumption and data throughput, ensuring its readiness for long-term ambulatory monitoring.

RESULTS: The deployed models achieve real-time inference on an ARM Cortex-M33 with as little as 21.7 kB RAM and 265k MACs. After optimization, energy consumption is reduced to 5.51 mJ per inference. Compared with the original model, RAM usage is reduced by 53.6%, with only a 0.5% absolute decrease in accuracy (97.9% to 97.4%). Hardware-in-the-loop power profiling confirms significant efficiency gains, validating the clinical feasibility of the proposed selective offloading strategy.

CONCLUSION: A NAS-guided, deployment-centric pipeline-spanning architecture search, compression/mapping, and embedded power profiling enables accurate, real-time ECG classification within stringent wearable constraints. The selective-offloading strategy bridges the gap between laboratory algorithms and practical cardiac surveillance by providing a high-fidelity, low-power, and clinically-aware solution for continuous arrhythmia screening.
journal: IEEE J Transl Eng Health Med

title: Differential effects of β1- and β2-adrenergic receptor block in long QT syndrome type 3: an in silico population study.
summary:
PURPOSE: Long QT syndrome type 3 (LQT3) is caused by a gain-of-function mutation in the voltage-gated sodium channel Nav1.5, resulting in an increased late sodium current (INaL) that prolongs action potential duration (APD) and promotes the development of early afterdepolarizations (EAD). LQT3 is commonly treated with therapies involving β-adrenergic receptor blockers. However, recent studies suggest that β-blockers may not provide a beneficial clinical effect in LQT3 patients, potentially explaining the increased risk of mortality during cardiac events compared to other long QT subtypes. This study investigates the underlying mechanisms of selective β-receptor block using a population-based computational approach.

METHODS: A population of 983 virtual human ventricular myocytes with enhanced INaL (representing LQT3) simulated, enabling electrophysiological and β-adrenergic analysis under conditions of varying degrees of β1- and β2-block. Susceptibility to arrhythmic events was quantified via APD prolongation or occurrence of EADs, and differences in susceptibility pathways, phosphorylation states, and ion current conductances were analyzed between susceptible and non-susceptible subpopulations.

RESULTS: Our results demonstrate that β1-block increases susceptibility, primarily via reduced IKs phosphorylation. In contrast, full β2-block reduces susceptibility, primarily via reduced ICaL phosphorylation, while partial β2-block does not. Differences in ionic current conductances in the susceptible and non-susceptible sub-populations are consistent with β-block driving imbalances in depolarizing and repolarizing currents.

CONCLUSIONS: Our findings motivate the development and preclinical testing of more selective β2-blocking agents, which could improve therapeutic outcomes in LQT3 patients.

title: RyR2-Mediated Ca 2+ Leak Drives Progressive Arrhythmogenic Cardiomyopathy.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Abnormal sarcoplasmic reticulum (SR) Ca 2+ release through ryanodine receptor 2 (RyR2) is a well-established mechanism of ventricular arrhythmias. Whether persistent RyR2 dysfunction can also initiate the structural remodeling characteristic of arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy (ACM) remains unknown. We tested the hypothesis that chronic RyR2-mediated Ca 2+ leak is sufficient to couple electrical instability to progressive cardiomyopathy.

METHODS: We generated a rabbit carrying the severe gain-of-function RyR2-V2475F mutation and characterized disease progression using longitudinal cardiac phenotyping, continuous electrocardiographic monitoring, cellular electrophysiology and Ca 2+ imaging, histopathology, biochemical analyses, and single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq). Therapeutic potential was evaluated by continuous treatment with the selective RyR2 inhibitor ent -verticilide for two months.

RESULTS: RyR2-V2475F rabbits developed spontaneous ventricular tachyarrhythmias, sudden cardiac death, and progressive right ventricular (RV)-dominant fibrofatty cardiomyopathy recapitulating major features of human ACM. Malignant ventricular arrhythmias preceded overt structural remodeling and were associated at the cellular level with early spontaneous Ca 2+ release and early afterdepolarizations. Early disease was characterized by remodeling of excitation-contraction coupling with preserved SR Ca 2+ load and contractile function despite RyR2 dysfunction; upon disease progression, these compensatory changes were accompanied by SR Ca 2+ depletion, impaired RV contractility and reduced left ventricular filling. Single-nucleus transcriptomics identified early fibroblast expansion and predicted cardiomyocyte-centered paracrine signaling before advanced fibrofatty infiltration. Cardiomyocytes also exhibited an altered lipid-metabolic transcriptome and intracellular lipid accumulation, accompanied by enhanced mitochondrial Ca 2+ uptake. Selective RyR2 inhibition markedly reduced ventricular tachycardia burden and preserved RV contraction and LV filling during disease progression.

CONCLUSIONS: Severe RyR2 gain-of-function can lead to both malignant ventricular arrhythmias and progressive arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy in a large-animal model, establishing persistent intracellular Ca 2+ dysregulation as a mechanistic link between electrical and structural heart disease. The ability of selective RyR2 inhibition to suppress arrhythmias and preserve cardiac function identifies RyR2 as a potentially actionable therapeutic target in arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy.

title: Optimized Strategy for Improving the Accuracy of Determining Left Bundle Branch Capture.
summary:
BACKGROUND: The accuracy of current ECG criteria for left bundle branch (LBB) pacing (LBBP) remains inadequate.

OBJECTIVES: To establish an optimized strategy to distinguish LBBP from left ventricular septal pacing (LVSP) in patients with a narrow QRS complex.

METHODS: LBBpo-V6RWPT, Native-V6RWPT, and Paced-V6RWPT were measured from LBB potential (LBBpo) onset, intrinsic QRS onset, and stimulus end to the R-wave peak in V6, respectively. ΔV6RWPT and ΔLBBpo-V6RWPT were defined as Paced-V6RWPT minus Native-V6RWPT and Paced-V6RWPT minus LBBpo-V6RWPT. Receiver operating characteristic analysis identified optimal cut-offs for these two differences, Paced-V6RWPT, and the V6-V1 interpeak interval in patients with transition-confirmed capture. Areas under the curves (AUCs) were compared by LBBpo status.

RESULTS: LBBP was confirmed in 292 (61.6%) of 474 patients with LBBAP. The optimal cut-off values of ΔLBBpo-V6RWPT, ΔV6RWPT, Paced-V6RWPT, and the V6-V1 interpeak interval for determining LBBP were 6 ms, 30 ms, 67 ms, and 31 ms, respectively. In 211 of 292 patients, LBBpo was recorded and the ΔLBBpo-V6RWPT criterion achieved the largest AUC (1.000), with 98.5% sensitivity and 99.5% specificity. LBBP was misclassified as LVSP by the ΔV6RWPT criterion in 3 patients but was correctly identified by the ΔLBBpo-V6RWPT criterion. In 81 of 292 patients, LBBpo was not recorded and the ΔV6RWPT criterion showed the largest AUC (0.990), with 98.8% sensitivity and 97.3% specificity.

CONCLUSIONS: Selecting ΔLBBpo-V6RWPT for patients with LBBpo and ΔV6RWPT for those without LBBpo may help classify LBB capture in unclassified LBBAP with narrow QRS complexes. Diagnostic accuracy in this population requires prospective validation.
